book.title: Adult Children of Emotionally Immature Parents
book.author: Lindsay C. Gibson

confidence_note: Healing fantasy (continuing to believe the parent will eventually change and give validation and love), first step of reconnecting with the authentic self and true feelings, relating to rather than being embedded in the parent, entering each interaction with a clear goal, the exercise of reflecting on a past bad conversation, and using understanding of why the parent behaves as they do to guide how much to engage come from a summary preview; book text not read. Old-text 'reparenting', 'inner child' and the three-layer healing structure are not confirmed and were dropped; the title changed accordingly.
facts: Many adult children hold a healing fantasy: they keep believing the parent will eventually change and give validation and love.
First step of healing: connect with the authentic self and true feelings.
Aim to relate to the parent rather than be embedded in the relationship.
Enter each interaction with a clear goal.
Exercise: reflect on a past bad conversation and name the goal you could have brought to it.
Understanding why the parent behaves as they do can guide how much you engage.
scene_details: a single goal for one interaction
tension: Waiting for the parent to change versus deciding what you want from the next conversation.
opening_idea: The exercise of replaying a bad conversation with a goal.

lessons.idea: Bring one goal of your own into a hard conversation.
lessons.anchor: Gibson: enter each interaction with a clear goal; relate to rather than be embedded.
lessons.everyday_example_idea: A man phones his father weekly hoping for approval and always leaves empty.

reflect_final: In your next hard conversation with a family member, what single goal could you set that does not depend on them changing?

use_cases.situation: A difficult call with a parent
use_cases.move: Choose one goal beforehand, such as finishing in ten minutes without arguing.

use_cases.situation: A friend keeps hoping a parent will change
use_cases.move: Ask what they want from the next visit.

use_cases.situation: Looking back on a bad talk
use_cases.move: Write the goal you could have brought.

pocket_idea: Replace waiting for them to change with a goal you can reach in the next conversation.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: The healing fantasy keeps people waiting.
